draft.title: Farming innovations
card: Farming innovations are new or improved methods that help farmers work around environmental limits, such as little rain or poor soil. They do not remove the limits, but they reduce their effect on yields.
Drip irrigation
pipes with small holes drip water slowly onto the soil near plant roots. Less water is lost to evaporation and runoff, so it helps in dry areas.
Crop rotation
growing different crops in the same field in turn, season after season. This helps keep the soil fertile and can break the cycle of pests and diseases that target one crop.
Stubble mulching
leaving crop stalks on the field after harvest. The cover shades the soil, holds in moisture and slows erosion by wind and water.
draft.remember: Innovations such as drip irrigation, crop rotation and stubble mulching reduce the limits that the environment puts on farming.

a.q: A farmer in a dry part of South Australia leaves wheat stalks on the paddock after harvest. How does this help?
opts: It holds moisture in the soil and slows erosion
It lets the farmer grow a different crop each year
It delivers water slowly to the roots of each plant
It mixes two crops in the same paddock at once
a.why: Leaving stalks on the field is stubble mulching. The cover shades the soil, keeps moisture in and slows erosion. Crop rotation is the method that changes the crop each season, so that option describes a different innovation.
a.clue: The stalks stay on the ground as a cover.

b.q: Tane grows tomatoes on dry, sandy land in Western Australia. Water is scarce and much of it evaporates. Which change best reduces this limit?
opts: Installing drip irrigation to water the plant roots
Growing a different crop in the paddock each season
Leaving the paddock empty so that pests die out
Ploughing the soil more often before each planting
b.why: Drip irrigation puts small amounts of water near the roots, so less is lost to evaporation. Crop rotation helps soil fertility and pests, but it does not stop water from evaporating, so it does not fix the main limit here.
b.clue: The problem is water lost before plants can use it.

proposal.title: Farming innovations
card: Farming innovations are new or improved methods that help farmers work around environmental limits, such as low rainfall or poor soil. They do not remove the limits, but they reduce their effect on yields.
Water limits
Drip irrigation drips water slowly from pipes onto the soil near plant roots, so less is lost to evaporation and runoff. Drought-resistant crops are varieties bred to grow and yield with less water.
Soil limits

Crop rotation grows different crops in a field in turn, which helps keep soil fertile and breaks pest cycles. Stubble mulching leaves crop stalks on the field after harvest to hold in moisture and slow erosion.
Intercropping
growing two or more crops in the same field at the same time, such as beans between rows of maize. It makes better use of the space, and if one crop fails the other may still yield.
proposal.remember: Innovations work around limits such as dry weather and poor soil, so farms can keep producing food.
